description: <div class="content-intro"><h2><strong>About InstaLILY</strong></h2> <p><a href="https://portal.instalily.ai/i/homepage" target="_blank">InstaLILY</a> is an AI products and infrastructure company that puts execution at the frontier of enterprise AI. It does not leave when the work ships; it stays and keeps the software working as the business changes. Lily runs wherever the work happens, in the cloud, on-premise, or at the edge, through InstaLILY's Small Data Center, built with NVIDIA technology. Founded in 2023 by Amit Shah and Sumantro Das, InstaLILY has raised nearly $100 million from Energize Capital, Insight Partners, and Home Depot Ventures. Headquartered in New York, with offices in San Francisco, London, and Toronto, InstaLILY serves leading companies across construction, industrial distribution, logistics, healthcare, and other operationally intensive industries. Learn more at <a href="https://instalily.ai/" target="_blank">https://instalily.ai/</a>.</p> <h3><strong>The Traction</strong></h3> <p>Revenue grew 5x over the past year, and Lily has driven over $200M in new annual sales for a single customer. Your code runs in live production systems inside billion-dollar operations, so you see your impact directly. People who do well here want that proximity to the work. title: Senior AI Engineer (GTM)
description: What do we do? Paddle offers digital product companies a completely different approach to their payment infrastructure. Instead of assembling and maintaining a complex stack of payments-related apps and services, we’re a Merchant of Record for our customers. That means we take away 100% of the pain of payment fragmentation. It’s faster, safer, cheaper, and, above all, way better. We’re backed by investors including KKR, FTV Capital, Kindred, Notion, and 83North and serve over 10,000 software sellers in 245 territories globally. The role: We’re looking for an entrepreneurial and technically strong Senior AI Engineer to join our Data & AI team and work with our Go-To-Market organisation. This is a builder's role, end to end. You’ll work closely with Marketing, Sales, and RevOps to solve high-value problems, design practical AI solutions and build them into reliable systems that people use every day. You’ll be expected to move comfortably from an ambiguous business challenge to a technical design, a working prototype, and then a production-ready solution. Your work could include building systems that segment and prioritise accounts, developing agents that automate sales workflows, or creating intelligent tools that help our teams research prospects and act on buying signals. You’ll own the full lifecycle of what you build, including evaluation, observability, reliability and cost optimisation. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys being close to users, can write production-quality code and is excited by the challenge of turning rapidly evolving AI capabilities into valuable commercial outcomes. Experience working with GTM teams is useful, but the ability to understand problems, build effective systems and measure their impact is more important. What you'll do: Design and build AI-powered systems for account segmentation, enrichment, scoring, prioritisation and buying-signal detection Develop and deploy agentic workflows for use cases such as account research, outbound personalisation, call summarisation and CRM hygiene Write production-quality code and build the integrations, data pipelines and services required to take solutions from prototype to reliable daily use Optimise systems for quality, latency and cost through evaluation, prompt design, model selection, routing, caching, context management and token optimisation Establish practical patterns for building AI systems at Paddle, including monitoring, guardrails, documentation and clear measures of business impact We'd love to hear from you if you: Have strong software engineering experience and can independently take a problem from technical design through to production; Python and SQL experience would be particularly relevant Have hands-on experience building applications with large language models, APIs, retrieval systems, agents or other applied AI technologies Understand how to evaluate and operate AI systems in production, including managing hallucination risk, latency, reliability, context limits and variable model costs Are comfortable working with structured and unstructured data, building integrations and turning information from multiple sources into useful systems Have an interest in commercial problems and can understand concepts such as ICP, segmentation, pipeline, buyer intent and sales workflows; direct GTM experience is beneficial but not essential Enjoy working directly with the people who use what you build, are comfortable with ambiguity and can balance speed, quality, and long-term maintainability Everyone is welcome at Paddle At Paddle, we’re committed to removing invisible barriers, both for our customers and within our own teams. We recognise and celebrate that every Paddler is unique and we welcome every individual perspective. As an inclusive employer, we don’t care if, or where, you studied, what you look like or where you’re from. We’re more interested in your craft, curiosity, passion for learning and what you’ll add to our culture. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t match every part of the job ad, especially if you’re part of an underrepresented group. Please let us know if there’s anything we can do to better support you through the application process and in the workplace. We will do everything we can to support any accommodations needed. We’re committed to building a diverse team where everyone feels safe to be their authentic self. Let’s grow together. Why you’ll love working at Paddle We’re a diverse, growing group of Paddlers who pride ourselves on our transparent, collaborative and respectful culture. We live and breathe our values, which are: Paddle Together - “None of us, is as smart as all of us” Paddle Simply - “Simple can be harder than complex: you have to get your thinking clean to make it simple” Paddle for others - “We can realise our wildest dreams, so long as we help enough other people to realise theirs” We offer a full suite of benefits, including attractive salaries, stock options, unlimited holidays, enhanced parental leave, retirement plans, private healthcare and well-being initiatives. We invest in learning and will help you with your personal development via constant exposure to new challenges, an annual learning fund, and regular internal and external training. Connecting at Paddle We’re a ‘digital-first’ company , which means our Paddlers always have the freedom to choose where, when and how they work within our hub locations. We recognize that where our Paddlers do their best work is unique to them and we provide trust and autonomy for everyone to work in a way which fits them best. We also value the power of connection and have invested in global hubs which help local communities flourish and bring us together for focused collaboration. Our Paddle hubs: In Europe: UK (London headquarters), Portugal (Lisbon hub), Netherlands and Ireland (Dublin hub) In North America: Austin, TX (USA) and Toronto (Canada) In APAC : Singapore Our hub philosophy creates an engaging experience for all Paddlers, wherever, whenever and however we choose to work. To support this, we focus hiring within our hubs and will always openly share the available locations for each open position on our job description. title: Head of Data Science

Our Merchant of Record model gives us a data position no PSP or billing provider has: subscription and pricing context alongside granular payment-outcome data, across thousands of software businesses. This role exists to turn that into economic value by putting machine learning and agentic systems into production. The mandate is deliberately narrow and deliberately ambitious: data science at Paddle owns automated decisioning inside the product — traditional machine learning and agentic systems alike — not decision-support analytics. We have a long list of candidate opportunities than we can fund, spanning payment performance and revenue recovery, sales and marketing operations, growth and monetisation intelligence, and risk, trust and compliance. We have a working hypothesis about which of these pays back first, and we'll share it — but part of the job in your first quarter is to pressure-test it, size the alternatives yourself, and tell us where to start. This is a founding role, and for the first few quarters it is a building role more than a managing one. You'll be the only person in the function: doing the analysis, engineering the features, training and evaluating the models or agents, taking the first system live with our engineering teams — and then operating it, answerable for its uptime, its drift and its numbers. Once the first use cases are proving out, you'll hire and lead a hub-and-spoke team of data scientists and machine learning engineers embedded across our highest-value business areas. You'll report into the VP of Data and work in close partnership with Product, Payments, Engineering, Risk and Finance. What you'll do: Prioritise which opportunities have the biggest impact.. Build a value-based use-case backlog across payment performance and revenue recovery, sales and marketing operations, growth and monetisation intelligence, and risk, trust and compliance; size the leading candidates properly; and make the call on sequencing with the relevant Product, Risk, RevOps and Finance stakeholders. This gets refreshed quarterly. Personally deliver the first system end to end: the analysis and back-test, the features, the model, policy or agent, the deployment, and the shadow and A/B tests that prove it works. Not a spec handed to someone else to build. Operate what you deploy. Own monitoring, retraining, drift response, incident handling and rollback for live decisioning, alongside the engineering teams whose services call it — and set the expectation that the function runs its systems rather than shipping them. Work across both traditional ML and agentic systems, and be honest about which a problem actually needs: a propensity or uplift model, a policy of rules, or an agent with tools, evals against golden answer sets and trace-level observability. Several of our strongest candidate use cases point each way. Build and lead the team — hire senior data scientists embedded in value areas and machine learning engineers in the hub, and set the professional standards, shared methods and reusable components the function runs on. Establish the production stack alongside Data Platform and Engineering: reproducible training data, code and artefacts; a model registry; inference services with real latency, availability and rollback requirements; historically accurate features where decisions need backdated reconstruction; eval harnesses and trace observability for agentic workflows; and monitoring for data quality, drift, model performance and economic outcomes. Start ad hoc where that's sufficient and platformise once the first use cases have shown what's actually needed. Own value capture end to end. Shadow-test and A/B test every deployment against the incumbent strategy, translate metric movement into a financial number on a methodology co-signed by Finance, and publish a quarterly report on realised value. Set the governance model for automated decisioning — proportionate risk assessment, clear ownership, latency and availability requirements, human escalation and rollback — working with Legal, Privacy, Compliance and Risk on GDPR, EU AI Act and payments obligations, and producing the evidence early enough to shape the design. Define the boundaries and the working relationship with Product Science, Analytics Engineering, Data Platform and AI Enablement, so accountability for decision support versus automated decisioning stays unambiguous. Deliver cross-functionally: embed in delivery groups with product owners, domain experts and platform engineers rather than handing models over the wall. Proofs of concept and dashboards are not what we're hiring for. Hands-on now, not formerly. Your first quarters are spent writing SQL and Python, engineering features, evaluating models and agents, and doing the work that gets a system live — not reviewing someone else's. Experienced across both traditional ML and agentic systems, and clear about how they differ in practice: propensity and uplift models, feature pipelines and drift on one side; tool and context design, prompt and retrieval iteration, evals against golden answer sets and trace observability on the other. Practised at running live systems rather than just launching them — monitoring, retraining, incident response, rollback, and the on-call reality of a decision the business depends on. Pragmatic about method: happy to argue for rules or heuristics where they capture most of the value, and to reserve models and agents for where they genuinely earn their keep. Comfortable with an undefined starting point. There's a long list of candidate use cases and a strong internal hypothesis, but no fixed roadmap — you'll be expected to form your own view, back it with numbers, and defend it to an executive audience. Strong on measurement — experimentation, uplift modelling, back-testing — and willing to hold your own work to a financial number that Finance will scrutinise. Able to hire, level and develop senior data scientists and ML engineers, and to set standards for a function that doesn't exist yet. Credible with executives and commercial stakeholders: you can take a use case from business problem to value estimate to prioritisation decision, and say no to low-value work. title: Chief of Staff

Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal to no prompting. Our first application is an agent-first mobile communication app. We believe building applications that users use daily for communication, coordination and collaboration needs will help integrate AI into their lives. The net effect is to eliminate misinformation, achieve low coordination costs, enable high quality tasks and collaboration at scale with minimal or little prompting. About the Role The Chief of Staff will drive major priorities across ActAI and its portfolio of businesses. title: Special Projects
description: Special Projects London (Shoreditch) | In person | Full time About Seamflow We're removing one of the last great barriers to progress in the physical world. Our vision is to unlock enormous value for Testing, Inspection, and Certification companies globally. The market is vast, the problem is real, and we're just getting started. We're rapidly growing following our 14x oversubscribed seed round backed by Tier 1 investors including Northzone and Initialized Capital. These funds backed the founders of Coinbase, Reddit, Klarna, and Spotify. We're growing very fast; demand is outstripping our supply, and we're building fast to keep up. The Team Our team includes AI researchers from world-leading academic institutions like Johns Hopkins, MIPT, Oxford, Cambridge and UCL, former founding engineers at unicorn startups, and alumni of X, Google, Amazon, and Yandex, alongside former leaders from McKinsey, BCG and Bain. We look for people who move fast, think clearly, and hold themselves to a high bar. The standard here is very high, and we're looking for someone who raises it further. The Role Special Projects sits directly alongside the CEO and Chief of Staff and takes on whatever the company needs most at that moment. There is no fixed remit and there is no playbook. One month that means preparing the material and the numbers behind a fundraise. The next it's working through legal, regulatory, and market access questions in a country we're entering, or holding an entire function open on your own until we've hired someone permanent into it. Whatever is broken, missing, or unowned lands here first. Be clear eyed about what this is. It is demanding, and a lot of it is unglamorous. Some of it is detail work that simply has to be right, with nobody available to check it behind you. What we need is a workhorse who is obsessive about detail, who closes things out rather than hands them back, and whose work nobody ever has to second guess. If that reads as a description of you rather than a warning, this is the highest leverage seat in the company for someone early in their career. You will be in the room for decisions most people see five years later. What We're Looking For 1–3 years in an environment with a high bar and short feedback loops: investment banking, strategy consulting, a fast growing startup, or something equally demanding we haven't thought of. An exceptional track record: We care that you were at the top of whatever room you were in, academically and professionally. AI-native: You already run your work through AI and operate at 10x as a result. You reach for these tools by default, not as a novelty, and you're constantly finding new ways to compress what used to take days into hours. Structured thinking: You break messy, ambiguous problems into parts, work out what actually matters, and sequence it. You can explain your reasoning on a whiteboard in two minutes. Ruthless organisation: Multiple workstreams, nothing dropped, nothing chased twice, everything written down. Strong with Excel, slides, and written communication: Most of our work travels as documents and models read by executives at large regulated businesses. Bias to action: You'd rather ship a good plan today than a perfect one next week. Work nobody has to check: You close the loop, catch your own mistakes, and flag the things you couldn't resolve rather than leaving them to be discovered. Someone who wants to be in the room, not on a call. This role is in-person, full time at our Shoreditch office. Nice to have: European languages, particularly German or French. title: Software Engineer (Frontend) - London
description: About Us Teton is redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology and a great product experience. As populations get older and staff shortages grow, healthcare systems are under pressure. Our mission is to decrease the cost of healthcare while improving the quality of care. Our product enables care teams to intervene, prevent and operate more efficiently. Our ambient sensors in resident rooms capture activity, sleep, respiration, gait and more. These signals are used both to react fast to risk events, like falls, and for long-term health analysis that care teams can act on. Teton is scaling fast, operating in the Nordics, UK, DACH and US. We recently raised a $20M Series A. Expect travel to the US to meet users and team members. We focus relentlessly on product excellence and user experience, deploying solutions at speed that make a tangible difference for carers. We are an aspiring meritocracy biased towards action, always striving to raise the bar. If you are driven by impact, speed and leveling up, this might be the place for you. If you are looking for a 9-17 job, perform best with structure and struggle dealing with unknowns, this is not for you. We believe close collaboration between a hard-working, high-agency team enables the fastest and most efficient iteration cycles, helping us build an impactful product that healthcare professionals truly love to use. The Job We're looking for an experienced Frontend Engineer to own customer-facing features from the first conversation with a care team to the feature running in production. Care workers rely on our product during every shift and care managers use it to follow up on their residents, on mobile and on the web. This isn't a ticket-taking role. You'll talk to users, cut scope, build the features, and check afterwards whether what you shipped actually made a shift easier. Alongside that, you'll help own the quality of how we build: the tests, pipelines and guardrails that let us ship fast without breaking what care teams depend on. In this role, you will focus on: Feature Development : Own features end-to-end, from design discussions through implementation to production rollout across multiple markets and languages, on the web app, the mobile app and the APIs behind them. Customer Insight : Talk to care staff and our customer success team every week, visit care facilities, and turn what you hear into clearly scoped product changes. Come with ideas, sketch the solution, and push it forward. Code Quality & Guardrails : Help own code quality across the frontend. Improve our CI/CD pipelines and automated tests, keep the infrastructure scalable, and build the guardrails that let AI coding agents contribute safely. Backend & APIs : Work with the APIs, data models and services your features need. You will not just consume APIs, you will help shape, improve and fix the systems behind them. Quality, Privacy & Safety : Ship with care for health data: sensible access control, auditability and privacy by default. Use staged rollouts so new features never get in the way of the alerts care teams depend on. Qualifications Several years of experience building production web applications. Strong TypeScript skills : this is the language for everything we build. Solid production experience with React on the web and/or React Native. Experience with CI/CD and automated testing, and a strong sense of what good code quality looks like. Great product taste and a keen eye for UX. You work well with designers and can make sensible design decisions yourself when needed. Comfortable talking directly with non-technical users and turning messy feedback into concrete decisions. Previous startup experience and/or shipping a product where you owned the outcome, from idea to adoption.X Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work both independently and in a team. Nice to Have Experience with React Native and Expo in production. Experience working with AI coding agents in a real codebase. AWS or equivalent cloud platform experience. Familiarity with TanStack, real-time systems or push notifications. Experience with health data or other regulated, privacy-sensitive domains (e.g. GDPR). What We Offer Participation in our warrant program (stock options). A small team where your decisions directly shape the product. A Copenhagen-based office with close collaboration, no async-only culture. Work on software that healthcare workers depend on every day, the impact is tangible and immediate. Join Our Team We're looking for individuals who share our vision and value ownership and entrepreneurship over a conventional job. At Teton, you'll have the chance to make a real impact with your work. If you're ready for more than just a job, come aboard and be part of our mission to transform healthcare. title: Tech Lead - New Customers Team
description: Tech Lead - New Customers Team Hybrid in London, UK We’re looking for a Tech Lead You'll lead the engineering behind how new businesses become iwoca customers – the application they fill in, the checks they go through, and the offer they get. The company Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are. That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed. We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive. The team The New Customers team owns everything from a business's first application to a funded loan: the application flow, the logic that routes each application, the documents we ask customers for, and the models that set loan amounts and pricing. Its measure of success is the customer lifetime value it adds between sign-up and first loan. The team sets its own goals and direction. It brings together engineers, data scientists, and product and strategy people. It partners closely with credit risk on the trade-offs behind every lending decision. Knowledge sharing is central to how the team works, supported by regular forums to share findings, and dedicated research and development time. You'll lead two engineers and report to the head of engineering for iwoca's customer journey, from first application to repeat lending. The role As the Tech Lead, you'll spend most of your time building. The team is moving its offer logic out of a legacy monolith into a new service. You'll shape what the team builds, decide how to build it, and own what goes live. You'll set its engineering roadmap, including what to pull out of the monolith, what to rewrite, and in what order. You'll build the systems that let data scientists test new models on live applications. Some experiments run for years, until each loan reaches the end of its term. title: Partnerships Manager - M&A Platform
description: The company It's still difficult for business owners to sell their business, or buy others, in the sub-£10m enterprise value market. Information asymmetry, lack of knowledge and low transaction values make it hard, and most M&A firms shy away from the segment because they can't serve it profitably. A generation of owner-managers is approaching retirement, and most of them have no realistic route to a sale. manda exists to fix that. We match buyers with sellers in the part of the market everyone else ignores, and we finance acquisitions ourselves so buyers arrive pre-qualified and often pre-financed. We've sold the first businesses, funded the first acquisition loans, and we're now opening the platform up beyond the businesses that already bank with us. manda is part of iwoca, one of Europe's leading fintech lenders. Since 2012 iwoca has provided more than £4 billion in funding and its mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments. That backing is why we can serve this market where others can't: a deep footprint in the SME economy with 150,000+ UK customers, the data and infrastructure of an established lender, and the ability to build clean, automated processes instead of running an advisory firm on spreadsheets. We’re looking for a Partnership Manager - manda (iwoca's M&A Platform) We're looking for someone to build the introducer network that brings business owners to manda, iwoca's M&A platform. Accountants, solicitors, wealth managers and brokers meet an owner who is thinking about retiring long before we do. Your job is to make sure that when they do they think of us, and that referring us is the easiest thing they do that day. The role Your mission is to build a referral channel that produces a steady flow of business owners who are genuinely ready to sell. Today almost all of our sellers come from iwoca's own customer base, found by hand and worked one at a time. That works, but the pool is finite. The professionals who already advise business owners are the most credible route to the ones we'd otherwise never reach, and right now we have no systematic way of working with them. You'll be starting from close to nothing, so the first version of this channel is yours to design. It also means the job is as much about making referrals actually arrive as it is about signing partners up. It also has to scale. In this industry most partner flow still depends on people turning up at industry events, which works but stops the moment you stop showing up. We're after the version of this channel where referring a client to manda takes a couple of clicks inside the software an adviser already uses. Key responsibilities include: Build the introducer network Find and win the firms worth working with: accountancy practices, corporate finance boutiques, solicitors, wealth managers and business transfer agents. Work out which kinds of firm actually refer, and concentrate there. Do the outbound yourself. Identify the firm, get the meeting, make the case, and follow up until something happens. Design what we offer them: how a referral is made, what the partner gets, what we commit to in return, and how we keep them informed once their client is with us. Make referrals actually arrive A signed partnership is worth nothing until a referral comes through. You'll own the ongoing relationship work that turns agreements into a flow: regular contact, keeping manda front of mind, briefing partner teams, and being the person they call. Track referral volume and quality by partner, and be honest about which relationships aren't working so we can stop spending time on them. Make the channel scale Judge every partnership by whether it adds referrals without adding work. A relationship that only produces when you're in the room isn't a channel yet. Work out which partner technology is worth plugging into: the practice management and accounting software advisers already work in, tracked referral links and partner portals, and integrations that let a firm refer a client without leaving their own tools. You won't build these yourself, but you'll identify them, make the commercial case, and scope them with our Product Builder. Look for partners who can bring a book rather than one client at a time. One firm with hundreds of owner-managed clients is worth more to us than ten firms with five, if we can find a way to surface the right candidates across the whole book. Work iwoca's existing network iwoca already has a broker network and a partnerships function with relationships across the SME economy. Working out where manda fits into those relationships is far faster than starting cold, and it's the first place to look. Events and community Build a focused programme of events worth attending and, where it makes sense, running our own: succession and exit planning, accountancy and adviser events, industry gatherings, and business owner peer communities. Judge them on referrals rather than attendance, and stop going to the ones that don't produce. Events are how you find and land partners, not how the channel scales. Prove the channel pays Establish what a referral actually costs us once your time, any partner incentives and events are counted, and how many convert into a signed mandate. We have an assumption in our financial model and nobody has yet tested it. The requirements We look for people who are smart, humble, motivated and who are always looking to improve. Essential: Around 4+ years in partnerships, channel or business development, ideally B2B, where you built or substantially grew a referral channel rather than inheriting one that already worked. You've done the full cycle yourself: identified the target firms, got the meetings, agreed the terms, and then managed the relationship afterwards. A background in M&A, marketplaces, business broking or business transfer. You understand that the work starts after the agreement is signed, and you have the discipline to keep a channel warm over months rather than weeks. Numerate and honest about performance. You track referrals by partner, you know which relationships are producing, and you say so when one isn't. You think in systems as well as relationships. You can tell the difference between a partnership that scales and one that only works while you're pushing it, and you'd rather replace your own manual work with an integration than defend it. Comfortable specifying technology without building it. You can look at a partner's tools and our product, work out what would make us the path of least resistance, and scope it clearly enough for a product team to build. Genuinely hands-on. There's no team to delegate to: you'll build the target list, send the emails, run the meetings and keep the CRM straight yourself. A commercial thinker with a bias for action, comfortable navigating ambiguity in an early-stage venture. Bonus: Experience with accountancy, legal or wealth management channels specifically. Experience running an event programme with commercial targets attached to it. Familiarity with the UK succession and exit planning landscape. Comfortable treating a CRM as a discipline rather than an afterthought, ideally HubSpot. You've shipped a partner integration, an embedded referral flow or a software marketplace listing, or worked closely with a product team on one. Familiar with the software UK accountancy practices and advisers actually work in, such as Xero, QuickBooks, Sage, IRIS or Dext. The salary We expect to pay £55,000–£80,000 and an annual performance based bonus for this role. But, we're open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews. The culture At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time. description: Keyloop bridges the gap between dealers, manufacturers, technology suppliers and car buyers. We empower car dealers and manufacturers to fully embrace digital transformation. How? Thorough understanding of the automotive finance customer lifecycle, including origination, contract management, end-of-contract customer journey, and retention and trade cycle management. Experience selling SaaS/cloud-based solutions. Proven track record in account management, ideally managing senior corporate stakeholders within financiers. Measure and report on the effectiveness of marketing campaigns and events, using data to support decisions and improve future marketing strategies. We build the systems and tools that power acquisition, retention, and overall subscription growth at scale. The Messaging Platform powers Spotify’s communications to over a billion users — from push notifications to emails and in-app messages that connect listeners to the content they love. Within this space, the Paloma squad focuses on message optimization: deciding which message reaches which user, through which channel, and at what moment. We’re evolving how messaging works at Spotify — moving from short-term optimization toward systems that understand long-term user journeys. By combining reinforcement learning approaches with deeper domain signals, we’re expanding how machine learning shapes the entire messaging funnel. What You'll Do Design, build, and ship machine learning models that optimize messaging across push, email, and in-app channels Plan and run A/B experiments in a multi-objective environment, balancing conversion, engagement, retention, and reachability Contribute to reinforcement learning systems that optimize for long-term user outcomes rather than immediate interactions Partner with product managers, data scientists, and engineers to define what success looks like and how to measure it Own the full ML lifecycle, from data and modeling to deployment, monitoring, and iteration Integrate ML models with upstream systems, including domain value signals and opportunity generation frameworks Help shape the future of AI-assisted development within the team, exploring how tools can accelerate experimentation and delivery Who You Are You have strong experience building and deploying machine learning models in production environments at scale You are comfortable translating business problems into ML solutions and discussing trade-offs with cross-functional partners You have worked on complex optimization problems such as ranking systems or multi-objective decision-making You bring hands-on experience with PyTorch and distributed systems such as Ray or similar frameworks You understand experimentation deeply and can design reliable tests in environments with interacting metrics You are able to analyze results using approaches like causal inference or metric decomposition when needed You have experience with or curiosity about reinforcement learning and long-term optimization systems You enjoy working across disciplines and navigating ambiguity while shaping strategy and direction Where You'll Be This role is based in London and Stockholm We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! title: Senior Digital Learning Experience Designer, Learning & Inclusion
description: We’re looking for a Senior Digital Learning Experience Designer to join our Learning & Inclusion team, the group responsible for creating learning experiences that help every Spotify band member grow, belong, and do their best work. You’ll bring together instructional design, visual design, storytelling, and broader learning and development expertise to create inclusive and effective experiences at scale. You’ll partner with subject-matter experts, people leaders, and Learning & Inclusion colleagues on company-wide initiatives, from leadership development to programs that bring Spotify’s values to life. What You'll Do Lead the end-to-end design of learning experiences, from needs analysis and curriculum architecture through development, launch, and evaluation. Partner with subject-matter experts and stakeholders to identify performance needs and turn them into clear learning objectives and practical solutions. Design learning journeys across live, digital, blended, and self-directed formats using evidence-based learning principles. Create engaging learning materials, including eLearning, facilitator guides, participant resources, job aids, presentations, and micro-learning experiences. Use visual design and storytelling to make complex ideas clear, memorable, and engaging while creating experiences that feel unmistakably Spotify. Build interactive digital learning experiences using AI-assisted workflows and authoring tools such as Articulate Storyline or Rise, Adobe Captivate, or similar platforms. Design inclusive learning experiences that reflect different perspectives, reduce barriers to participation, and support a culture of belonging. Pilot and iterate on learning experiences using learner feedback, stakeholder input, and performance data. Define meaningful measures of success and evaluate learning effectiveness, knowledge transfer, learner experience, and behavior change. Manage multiple learning projects from initial scoping through delivery while creating clarity around priorities, timelines, and stakeholder expectations. Explore emerging approaches in learning design, including AI-assisted authoring and adaptive learning, and apply them where they can meaningfully improve the learner experience. Who You Are You have 5+ years of professional instructional design experience and a portfolio demonstrating thoughtful work across multiple learning formats. You apply learning science principles such as cognitive load, retrieval practice, spaced learning, and adult learning theory to practical design decisions. You know how to uncover learning and performance needs, translate them into measurable objectives, and design learning journeys that build knowledge and skills over time. You create meaningful practice through scenarios, simulations, assessments, and other interactive experiences rather than relying on passive content. You have strong visual and UX design judgment and understand how typography, hierarchy, layout, and visual storytelling can make learning clearer and easier to navigate. You have experience with rapid authoring tools such as Articulate 360, Captivate, Lectora, or similar platforms, along with design tools such as Figma, Adobe Creative Suite, Canva, or equivalent. You can create clear storyboards, scripts, facilitator guides, and supporting materials that help others confidently deliver consistent learning experiences. You use learner feedback and data to evaluate effectiveness, iterate on your work, and connect learning experiences to meaningful outcomes. You communicate complex ideas clearly and collaborate effectively with subject-matter experts, leaders, and cross-functional partners. You’re comfortable navigating ambiguity, balancing multiple priorities, and taking ownership from an early idea through a polished learning experience. You bring experience in areas such as inclusive learning design, leadership development, learning technology, short-form learning video or animation, LMS/LXP platforms, or SCORM/xAPI. You have a degree in instructional design, learning sciences, education, human-computer interaction, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience. title: Engineering Manager - Data Platform
description: Within the Data Platform studio, we own two critical pillars: our event delivery platform that collects trillions of events per day from producers to consumers, and another, which handles the pseudonymisation of data so Spotify can use data responsibly and in compliance with privacy regulations. These systems sit at the heart of Spotify's data collection and are used by hundreds of teams across the company. We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a team of six experienced engineers distributed across Europe. You'll set the technical direction, ensure the team delivers high-impact work, and - just as importantly - invest deeply in the growth and careers of your engineers. If you're energised by both the technical challenges of large-scale data systems and the human side of building a high-performing team, we'd love to hear from you. What You’ll Do Lead and develop a team of six experienced engineers, with a strong focus on coaching, career development, and creating an environment where people do the best work of their careers. Take accountability for the team's delivery, ensuring clear priorities, healthy execution, and measurable outcomes. Partner with product and stakeholders to shape the roadmap for event delivery and privacy infrastructure. Drive technical strategy and architectural decisions for systems operating at Spotify scale. Build a culture of ownership, psychological safety, and continuous improvement. Collaborate across Data Platform and the wider engineering organisation to align on shared goals and dependencies. Manage on-call health, operational excellence, and reliability for the team's services. Actively participate in hiring, onboarding, and growing the team's capabilities. Who You Are You have experience managing teams of senior/experienced engineers and understand that people leadership is your primary craft, not a side responsibility. You hold yourself and your team accountable for outcomes, not just activity. You communicate clearly and build trust across functions and time zones. title: Member of Technical Staff
description: Slingshot AI Slingshot AI is the team behind Ash, the first AI designed for mental health. Our mission is to make support more accessible and help people change their lives in the ways they want. We’re building a world-class team by empowering individuals with the autonomy, flexibility, and support they need to do their best work. We dream big, iterate fast, and care deeply. If that sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you. Our team spans machine learning, product, engineering, conversational design, clinical, growth, and operations, with offices in both New York City and London. We're a well-funded Series A company, having raised $93M from Andreessen Horowitz, Radical Ventures, Forerunner Ventures, plus top-tier tech investors involved in ElevenLabs, Captions, Shopify, Plaid, Notion, Canva, Twitch, Airtable, and many others. Slingshot AI is the team behind Ash, the first AI designed for mental health. Our mission is to make support more accessible and help people change their lives in the ways they want. We’re building a world-class team by empowering individuals with the autonomy, flexibility, and support they need to do their best work. We dream big, iterate fast, and care deeply. If that sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you. Our team spans machine learning, product, engineering, conversational design, clinical, growth, and operations, with offices in both New York City and London. We're a well-funded Series A company, having raised $93M from Andreessen Horowitz, Radical Ventures, Forerunner Ventures, plus top-tier tech investors involved in ElevenLabs, Captions, Shopify, Plaid, Notion, Canva, Twitch, Airtable, and many others. The role As a Member of Technical Staff focused on Machine Learning, you will ship models, training infrastructure, harnesses and evals end-to-end: designing, building, and launching the tech that makes Ash differentiated as a specialized model for mental health, to change a billion minds and lives. As a core member of a small but highly skilled team, we expect you to act as an owner and to care passionately about delivering value to our users and ultimately to make people's lives better. We are looking for builders who care deeply about the quality of their work and want to ship things that make a real difference in people's lives. We care more about how you think and build than your specific background. If you're a great engineer who's curious about ML, we'd love to hear from you. We work on a model-agnostic post-training engine running on our own cluster of leased GPUs managed by SkyPilot, trained by an auto-research loop, and evaluated with our home-grown eval index aimed specifically at mental health. We’re constantly improving, and focus on building feedback loops over features, and constantly learning from our production performance, our psych research team, and scalable data sources. Our product tech stack uses Dart/Flutter for the app, Kotlin for core backend services, and Next.js/TypeScript for internal tooling, as well as Rust for low level media streaming. We use gRPC and GCP (Kubernetes, Cloud Run) as our primary cloud provider. You're not required to be an expert in all of these tools, but we would like you to come with a learning mindset and to not be afraid of getting your hands dirty with whatever tool the job might require. About you 3+ years of engineering experience, owning systems other people rely on. Experience working with LLMs, ideally with fine-tuning, harness engineering, and evals Proficient in using agents to do your homework for you Driven by creating a world-class product with a world-class team, want to own what you build, and you're happy tearing down experiments and features as we learn Experience in a fast-paced startup, or the drive to thrive in one. Collaborative and direct. You enjoy working in person with a small team. title: Senior Campaign Operations Manager
description: OUR MISSION To become the car-changing destination of choice. By combining technology, media and deep automotive expertise, we've turned how people buy, sell, advertise and lease cars on its head. What started as a simple reviews site is now one of the largest online car-changing destinations in Europe. Last year alone we grew over 50% with nearly £3bn worth of cars bought on site, while £1.8bn of cars were listed for sale through our Sell My Car service. In 2024 we went big and acquired Autovia - creators of AutoExpress and Evo magazines - doubling our audience overnight. Together we now have one of the biggest YouTube channels in the world with almost 10m subscribers and over 1.1 billion annual views, while we sell 1.2 million print copies of our magazines and have an annual web content reach over 350million. And we’re a long way from done! CAMPAIGN OPERATIONS @ CARWOW The Campaign Operations team sits at the heart of Carwow’s OEM and Media business. We turn ambitious commercial ideas into high-quality digital advertising campaigns that deliver strong results for our clients and meaningful revenue for Carwow. We work closely with Sales, Product, Data, Marketing, Engineering, editorial and external partners to deliver campaigns across Carwow’s automotive media portfolio. Our mission is to make campaign delivery accurate, efficient and scalable while continuously improving how we work through better processes, technology and innovation. YOUR MISSION As a Senior Campaign Operations Manager, your role will be split roughly equally between two areas: campaign delivery, and ad tech. Campaign delivery (around 50%): You’ll own the delivery and optimisation of client advertising campaigns across Carwow Studio brands and Carwow. You’ll make sure campaigns launch accurately, perform against their KPIs and give clients an excellent experience after the sale. Ad tech and data (around 50%): You’ll be the team’s go-to expert for our advertising technology and campaign data. You’ll lead the troubleshooting of ad serving, creative rendering, tracking and data discrepancy issues. You’ll also maintain and improve our ad tech setup and the data flows that power our reporting. Working with Product, Engineering and Data teams, you’ll help develop and integrate new tools, features and automated reporting. Success in this role means consistently delivering high-quality campaigns while building a reliable, efficient and scalable ad tech and data foundation for Campaign Operations. The role offers a clear path to progress to IC4 Campaign Operations Specialist. WHAT YOU'LL DO Campaign delivery Own the end-to-end delivery of advertising campaigns across channels, from planning and setup through to optimisation, reporting and post-campaign analysis. Ensure campaigns are implemented accurately, launched on time and delivered in line with agreed objectives and KPIs. Monitor performance and lead optimisation with internal teams and clients to meet and exceed campaign KPIs. Act as the primary point of contact for clients after the sale, covering campaign performance and technical questions. Produce high-quality reports and post-campaign analysis decks, and present findings and recommendations to internal stakeholders and clients. Identify commercial opportunities, such as upweights, extensions and optimisations, that deliver additional value for clients and Carwow. Ad tech and data Proactively troubleshoot technical issues across ad serving platforms, creative rendering, campaign tracking and data, minimising delivery and revenue risk. Lead ad tech projects, including implementing new tools, resolving ad server and reporting discrepancies and managing technical integrations. Maintain and improve our ad tech setup and the data flows behind campaign reporting, ensuring accuracy across internal and third-party sources. Partner with Product, Engineering and Data teams to develop and integrate new ad tech features, tools and automated reporting. Drive the adoption of automation, AI and new technology across Campaign Operations while maintaining strong quality-control standards. Continuously review processes to improve efficiency, accuracy and scalability, and share ad tech and data knowledge across the team. WHAT YOU'LL NEED Proven experience managing and delivering digital advertising campaigns within a publisher, media owner, agency or ad tech environment. Strong hands-on knowledge of Google Ad Manager, and experience with a range of creative formats including video, display and HTML5. Confidence troubleshooting technical issues across ad serving, creative rendering, tracking and reporting data. A solid understanding of programmatic advertising, yield management and optimisation techniques. Experience leading or contributing to ad tech or data projects, such as implementing new tools, resolving discrepancies or managing technical integrations. Strong analytical skills, with the ability to work across multiple data sources and turn campaign data into clear insights and recommendations. Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple campaigns, projects, stakeholders and deadlines at the same time. Strong attention to detail and a commitment to accurate, high-quality work in setup, troubleshooting and reporting. Confident communication and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to explain campaign performance and technical issues clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences. A commercially minded, collaborative approach and a genuine interest in improving processes through technology, data, automation and AI. BONUS POINTS Experience in the automotive, publishing or digital media industry. Certifications in Google Ad Manager, Google Ads, programmatic platforms or other ad tech tools. Experience with data and reporting tools such as BigQuery, SQL, Looker or similar. Knowledge of paid social, YouTube, off-site display or demand-generation and lead-generation campaigns. Familiarity with platforms such as DV360, Meta Ads Manager, Salesforce, Driftrock or audience-management platforms. Previous involvement in process-improvement, automation or AI projects. WHY THIS MIGHT NOT BE FOR YOU Campaign Operations is a fast-paced, high-pressure environment, with responsibility for delivering commercially important campaigns against tight deadlines and changing priorities. You’ll need to be comfortable managing multiple campaigns, taking ownership and proactively identifying potential issues before they affect delivery. title: Principal Counsel, Africa Legal
description: About Zipline Zipline is the world's largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world's largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world's largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we've built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people's lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About You and The Role Zipline is seeking a senior, strategic, and highly adaptable lawyer to lead and scale legal and compliance across multiple countries of operation in Africa. This role sits at the intersection of compliance execution and regulatory strategy and is critical to enabling Zipline's continued growth in complex and evolving regulatory environments. You will independently lead all Africa Legal & Compliance operations and strategy while serving as an integral member of Zipline International's high-impact Legal Team. You will also be a key member of the Zipline Africa Leadership Team, with the Heads of People and Finance and our Country Directors, and with a dotted reporting line to Zipline Africa's CEO. You will work cross-functionally with the Africa Leadership Team, Operations, Policy, Government Affairs, People, Finance, and Engineering, and will report directly to Zipline's Deputy General Counsel. This is a hands-on leadership role that offers the rare opportunity to build and shape the Legal function with significant autonomy, while benefiting from the collaboration and support of a larger global legal team. One day you may be advising on a complex Nigerian employment or a healthcare regulatory issue in Cote d'Ivoire; the next, developing compliance training for teams across Africa or helping the business navigate export controls, sanctions, anti-corruption, and other cross-border legal risks. What You'll Do Design, implement, scale, and continuously improve Zipline's legal and compliance programs across Africa, with a focus on sustainable, practical operations that support rapid growth Lead day-to-day compliance workstreams covering sanctions, anti-bribery and anti-corruption, privacy, healthcare, employment, and product-related regulations Support internal investigations, audits, and risk assessments, partnering closely with People, Finance, and senior leadership Manage litigation and disputes across Zipline's African markets Translate complex regulatory requirements into clear, actionable guidance for business and technical teams Own compliance with U.S. government award requirements, including FARs and 2 CFR 200, and serve as a primary point of contact for U.S. government contracting officers (including at the U.S. Department of State) Monitor and assess regulatory and policy developments across relevant African jurisdictions and advise leadership on emerging risks and opportunities Cross-Functional Partnership & Culture Act as a senior legal advisor to business leaders, providing pragmatic, risk-calibrated guidance Build strong relationships across the company and help foster a durable "culture of compliance" where teams understand the rules of the road and feel empowered to raise issues early Help shape Zipline's long-term legal and regulatory strategy in Africa, balancing compliance rigor with innovation and speed What You'll Bring A willingness to dive deep into unfamiliar issues and operate effectively in ambiguous, fast-environments Strong judgment and the confidence to make independent decisions, coupled with the discernment to escalate when appropriate Experience advising on legal and compliance matters, preferably in international or emerging-market environments The ability to break down complex legal and regulatory problems into clear priorities and practical solutions Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to advise senior stakeholders A collaborative, solutions-oriented mindset and strong organizational skills Willingness to travel up to ~25% to Africa and San own sensibilities. This stage also covers refactoring, optimisation and a first-pass ontology that lays the foundation for AI use cases. Validate: Reconciliation architecture and row-level sign-off, so every migration is provably correct. The first part is delivery excellence that compounds . You’ll make sure every migration we deliver is better than the last. That means defining the standards, building the playbooks and reusable assets, and turning the lessons from each strategic engagement into capability across the practice. You’ll also develop the engineers and leads who carry that standard across AMER, EMEA and APAC. The second part is commercial impact . You’ll turn delivery quality into a competitive edge: faster delivery, sharper scoping and pricing, and healthy margins you can measure and report on. Working closely with Sales and Solution Engineering, you’ll shape the offer that makes Infinite Lambda the obvious choice for enterprise migration, anywhere in the world. Responsibilities 1. Practice and standards Be the person engineers, sales and clients ask when a migration question is hard: what to migrate first, what to refactor and what to move as is, and how to resolve conflicting logic. Own the migration standard for Assess, Convert and Validate. This covers reference architectures, sequencing, reconciliation and stage-gate checklists, and what we won’t do. Make sure Fast and Deep Discovery produce a defensible estimate, a dependency map and early red flags before we commit to a fixed price. Hold the same quality bar in every region: conversion quality, reconciliation sign-off and post-go-live incidents. Keep the practice up to date as Flowline, the source parsers and the target platforms change (Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, Iceberg). 2. Knowledge, IP and the asset catalogue Join engagements at scoping and agree what each strategic migration should leave behind (patterns, decisions, failure modes, measurements) and who will capture it. Capture lessons at wave checkpoints, and close each engagement with a review of what worked, what didn’t, and what should change in the standard. Decide which lessons become reusable assets and which stay one-offs. Bring field requirements and recurring challanges to the Flowline product team, and move proven assets into Product & Services. 3. Formulate hypotheses around the products we build and seek the signal needed to validate them. Define what a correct result is for a given input and state, determine whether to assemble datasets from real usage or hand-written cases, and gate changes on regression results. Track and pull external datasets, models, and benchmarks from published research and open-source releases. Raise the bar on your team through code and design review, and bring other engineers up on eval practice. Some of the technical questions in this area are still open. You will help answer them. title: Director, Technical Account Management
description: <p>Datadog is seeking a Director, Technical Account Management (TAM) for the EMEA region to join our high-growth organization and world-class Technical Post Sales (TPS) Team. You will own the strategy, growth, and execution of a team of 25–30 today, with a clear mandate to scale to 50–70+ over the next two to three years. You will be building organizational infrastructure, developing first-line leaders, and establishing scalable processes before they're needed.</p> <p>TAMs are technical experts who provide paid "white glove" technical services to our largest customers, supporting adoption and providing guidance across the comprehensive Datadog product suite. A TAM is held in high regard as an expert and trusted advisor for how IT Operations translates to business value.</p> <p>This is a senior leadership role where you will set the technical post-sales vision for all of EMEA, own executive relationships with key accounts, evangelize the TPS offering at scale, and grow services revenue across the region.</p> <p><em>At Datadog, we place value in our office culture—the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.</em></p> <h2><strong>What You'll Do:</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Scale the EMEA TAM organization from 25–30 to 50–70+, hiring first-line leaders, designing team structures, and building systems that sustain quality through rapid growth.</li> <li>Lead a team of managers and senior TAM ICs across EMEA, ensuring customer success, retention, and expansion at high standards of technical delivery.</li> <li>Own the commercial strategy for the TPS program, partnering with Sales to position, price, and sell TAM services as a core part of the Datadog value proposition.</li> <li>Define and execute regional OKRs aligned with global TPS goals, driving accountability through your leadership team each quarter.</li> <li>Lead executive-level recruiting and build a leadership pipeline from within, developing managers who can in turn scale their own teams.</li> <li>Serve as executive sponsor for strategic EMEA accounts, engaging at the C-suite level to reinforce value, resolve escalations, and identify expansion opportunities.</li> <li>Partner with global TPS, Product, Sales Engineering, CS, and Enablement to standardize and evolve the TAM offering, customizing for regional needs where warranted.</li> <li>Establish operational rigor: clear metrics, health scorecards, capacity planning, and forecasting to give full visibility into team performance and customer outcomes.</li> <li>Drive talent development programs such as performance reviews & career growth plans, focusing on building future leaders within the organization and motivating, growing, & retaining top talent.</li> </ul> <p> </p> <h2><strong>Who You Are:</strong></h2> <ul> <li>8+ years leading Professional Services, TAM, have a track record of building leadership depth within your orgs.</li> <li>Commercially minded, with direct experience selling or co-selling services and a history of growing services revenue; you position TAM as a value driver, not a cost center.</li> <li>Technically fluent across infrastructure, cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP), observability, and monitoring, credible with practitioners and C-level executives alike.</li> <li>A strategic operator who pairs vision with execution: you set direction, build the systems to support it, and develop your team's ability to operate independently.</li> <li>3–5+ years earlier in your career as a TAM, Solutions Architect, or equivalent client-facing technical IC, giving you firsthand credibility with your team.</li> <li>Willing and able to travel up to 50% of the time across the EMEA region.</li> </ul> <p> </p> <h2><strong>Bonus Points:</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience redesigning organizational structures mid-growth: building new team shapes or specializations as a business scales.</li> <li>Track record evangelizing cloud adoption, observability, or security to C-level and board-level stakeholders across EMEA.</li> <li>Hands-on experience with Datadog or other leading cloud monitoring and observability platforms.</li> <li>Multilingual or deep experience navigating multi-cultural teams across EMEA markets.</li> title: Staff Software Engineer - Workloads
description: <div class="content-intro"><div> <div> <div class="gmail_quote"> <div> <div><span id="m_-113912706363268805m_-2746164444908759431gmail-docs-internal-guid-131e4fb0-7fff-b4e9-ff50-e8cf32449b1b">CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at <a href="https://www.coreweave.com">www.coreweave.com</a>.</span></div> <div> </div> <div>We're proud to be a Living Wage accredited Employer.</div> </div> </div> </div> </div> <p> </p></div><p><strong>About the Team</strong></p> <p>Launchables is CoreWeave's platform for building Physical Intelligence. We bring simulation, training and evaluation tools into a common platform, allowing robotics, autonomous systems and engineering teams to focus on their applications while Launchables handles common execution and infrastructure needs.</p> <p>We turn specialist Physical AI software into capabilities that researchers and engineers can use, adapt and build upon. Our work combines strong software engineering with applied domain knowledge to make complex workloads accessible, reproducible and useful in real-world environments.</p> <p>As a Staff Software Engineer, Workloads - Physical AI, you will develop engine integrations, application code, adapters, templates and developer tools that make specialist software available through Launchables. You will work directly with researchers and engineers to understand their tasks, assumptions, dependencies and expected outcomes, translating these into interfaces and configurations that preserve the capabilities they need.</p> <p>You will take ownership of how users configure, run, customise and evaluate workloads. This includes defining meaningful inputs, defaults, constraints and outputs; building command-line and API interfaces; and creating examples and documentation that help users extend existing templates or author their own. You will establish appropriate validation for packaging, execution and application outcomes, working with domain specialists to make evaluation criteria and their limitations clear.</p> <p>You will profile workloads to improve preparation time, GPU utilisation, concurrency and data movement while preserving the intended computation. You will also capture the inputs, versions, settings and execution conditions needed to reproduce runs, with logs, metrics and artefacts that help users diagnose failures, compare experiments and interpret results.</p> <p>Working alongside engineers responsible for the shared runtime and platform services, you will turn feedback from early users into better interfaces, defaults, tests and guidance. You will identify reusable patterns across integrations, shape shared platform capabilities, review designs and mentor colleagues. You will use coding agents and automation to accelerate development, applying the review, testing and domain judgement needed to ensure the resulting software behaves as intended.</p> <p><strong>Qualifications:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Strong software engineering skills, demonstrated through dependable software or developer tools used by other people.</li> <li>Applied depth in at least one relevant area, such as robotics simulation, autonomous-vehicle evaluation, reinforcement learning, synthetic-data generation or engineering simulation.</li> <li>Experience making specialist or research software usable beyond its original author, including configuration, testing, documentation and diagnosis.</li> <li>Sound judgement about experimental assumptions, evaluation criteria, reproducibility and the conclusions a result supports.</li> <li>Familiarity with containerised execution and experience tracing problems across application and infrastructure boundaries.</li> <li>Comfortable learning unfamiliar tools and domains, working closely with specialists and recognising when their expertise is needed.</li> <li>Evidence of improving shared tools or engineering practices across multiple projects, with clear reasoning about what should be common and what should remain application-specific.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Preferred Skills:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience developing software in Python, Go or C++.</li> <li>Familiarity with simulation and machine-learning frameworks.</li> <li>Experience profiling GPU workloads and identifying performance or resource bottlenecks.</li> <li>Experience with Kubernetes or workflow orchestration.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Wondering if you're a good fit?</strong></p> <p>We believe in investing in our people, and value candidates who can bring their own diversified experiences to our teams - even if you aren't a 100% skill or experience match. Here are a few qualities we've found compatible with our team. If some of this describes you, we'd love to talk.</p> <ul> <li>You enjoy turning specialist Physical AI software into dependable tools that other researchers and engineers can use independently.</li> <li>You care about making experiments understandable and reproducible, with clear evidence of what their results do and do not establish.</li> <li>You combine hands-on engineering with curiosity about unfamiliar domains, and enjoy helping colleagues build reusable, high-quality systems.</li> </ul> <p>We welcome relevant experience from industry, research engineering and academia. We are interested in what you have built, how others use it and the judgement you brought to making it work.</p> <p><strong>Why CoreWeave?</strong></p> <p>At CoreWeave, we work hard, have fun, and move fast! We're in an exciting stage of hyper-growth that you will not want to miss out on. We're not afraid of a little chaos, and we're constantly learning. Our team cares deeply about how we build our product and how we work together, which is represented through our core values:</p> <ul> <li>Be Curious at Your Core</li> <li>Act Like an Owner</li> <li>Empower Employees</li> <li>Deliver Best-in-Class Client Experiences</li> <li>Achieve More Together</li> </ul> <p>We support and encourage an entrepreneurial outlook and independent thinking. We foster an environment that encourages collaboration and enables the development of innovative solutions to complex problems. As we get set for takeoff, the organization's growth opportunities are constantly expanding. You will be surrounded by some of the best talent in the industry, who will want to learn from you, too. Come join us!</p> <p><em>The base salary range for this role is £116,000 to £155,000. The starting salary will be determined by job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and the market location. We strive for both market alignment and internal equity when determining compensation. In addition to base salary, our total rewards package includes a discretionary bonus, equity awards, and a comprehensive benefits program (all based on eligibility).</em></p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><em>To fulfill our obligation to protect client data, successful applicants offered employment with CoreWeave will be required to complete a basic criminal record check, conducted in compliance with GDPR. Employment offers are conditional upon receiving satisfactory check results.</em></p> <p><strong>What We Offer</strong></p> <p>In addition to a competitive salary, we offer a variety of benefits to support your needs, including:</p> <ul> <li>Family-level Medical Insurance</li> <li>Family-level Dental Insurance </li> <li>Generous Pension Contribution </li> <li>Life Assurance at 4x Salary </li> <li>Critical Illness Cover </li> <li>Employee Assistance Programme </li> <li>Tuition Reimbursement</li> <li>Work culture focused on innovative disruption</li> </ul> <p><em>Benefits may vary by location. </em></p> <p><strong>Equal Opportunity </strong></p> <p><em>CoreWeave is an equal opportunity employer, committed to fostering an inclusive and supportive workplace. All qualified applicants and candidates will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, disability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or genetic information.</em></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;"><strong>Recruitment Agencies</strong></span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;"><em><em data-stringify-type="italic">CoreWeave does not accept speculative CVs.
